title: Operators
hook: Operators are expressions with precedence. Null-coalescing and null-conditional are the ones that keep Redis lookups and token payloads from throwing. C# 14 lets `?.` sit on the left of an assignment.

sections.heading: Arithmetic, comparison, logical, assignment
sections.prose: Arithmetic: `+ - * / %` and increments. Integer `/` truncates toward zero — `5/2` is `2`, not `2.5`. Comparison and equality: `< > <= >= == !=`. For `string`, `==` is content equality (overloaded), unlike JS reference-or-coercion surprises. Logical: `& | ^ !` always evaluate both sides for bool; `&& ||` short-circuit — use those in guards. Assignment is right-associative (`a = b = 0`). Compound `+=` etc. exist. Precedence is the usual C family; parenthesize when mixing `??` with `?:`.

snippets.label: Null-coalescing and null-conditional
snippets.explanation: `??` supplies a fallback. `?.` skips member access. Null-conditional assignment (C# 14) does not evaluate the right-hand side when the receiver is null. `++`/`--` are still not allowed on `?.`.

sections.heading: C# 14 null-conditional assignment
sections.prose: Before C# 14 you wrote `if (msg is not null) msg.RetryCount = n;`. Now `msg?.RetryCount = n;` is legal, including `+=`. The right-hand expression runs only when the left receiver is non-null — important if the RHS hits Redis or deserializes a token. Do not confuse this with `??=`, which assigns when the left value is null.

interviewTakeaways: Integer division truncates; use decimal/double when you mean real division.
C# 14: `x?.Prop = expr` assigns only if `x` is not null; RHS is skipped otherwise.
commonPitfalls: Using `==` on floating point for money — use decimal and exact compares, or a tolerance for double.
Writing `x ?? y ?? z` then mixing with `?:` without parentheses.
Assuming `customer?.Order = GetOrder()` always calls `GetOrder` — it does not when customer is null.

jsTsCorrelations.note: JS has `??` and `?.`. Optional chaining on the left of assignment is a JS syntax error; C# 14 allows `x?.Prop = v`. JS `==` coerces; C# `==` does not.
